packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

reader: Claude Opus 5.5, fresh subagent, prompt and images only; repository and search tools available but forbidden; exposures stated in each response; packets 02 and 14 completed by further fresh readers after a display cap hid images, packet 17 reread by a fresh reader
text:
PACKET 12 - UNVERIFIED BLIND IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or reading of these fragments. The only identifying text I saw is the modern pencil shelfmark written on the fragments themselves ("Stams, STA, Frg. 257-2r", "-3v", "-4r", "-4v", "-5v", "-6r", "-6v", "-7v" etc.). I did not identify the work.

Beyond the rules: I opened only PROMPT.md and the image files (plus a directory listing of packet-12 to learn the filenames). To read the images I made temporary crops, enlargements and horizontal mirror-flips of the packet images in my session scratchpad (outside the repo). That is image processing, not a new source. Some image views were dropped from my context partway through. I re-viewed the parts I needed, but I did not look again at every right-column tile at full size (for example 021, 024, 027, 028, 030, 031). For those I worked from zoomed crops of the same tiles.

Line numbers: "L1, L2 ..." count text lines (text under the staves, not the neumes) from the top of the named image or tile. Where a text line is repeated in two overlapping tiles, I note that and do not count it twice.

======================================================================
LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
======================================================================

The packet shows four faces:

Face A (image-001 overview; tiles 002-009). A wooden board, probably a book cover board. The top and bottom edges have leather or metal clasp/strap remains. Near the right edge is a narrow vertical band of offset (transferred) ink: brown text letters, square black neume heads and red staff lines. It reads in mirror image, so it is a set-off from a leaf that was once pasted or pressed against the board, not original writing on the wood. There is a faint modern pencil note near the lower edge. Single column. Text alternates with neumes on red lines, so this is a notated chant leaf.

Face B (image-010 overview; tiles 011-018). The other side of the board, with strap or hinge remains along the right edge. I saw no text on it.

Face C (image-019 overview; tiles 020-031). One long vertical strip ("257-2r", about 2-3 cm wide, at left) and five small fragments ("257-3r" to "257-7r"). All are parchment with square (Gothic) chant notation on red-ruled lines. Text is in a Gothic textualis bookhand in brown ink. There are red rubrics and red initials, with red touching on some letters. The strip carries the left edge of a column, about 13 text lines plus notation. One large red initial "P" spans two lines.

Face D (image-032 overview, not available to me as an image; tiles 033-044). The reverse sides of the same pieces: "257-2v" strip (left), "257-3v", "257-4v", "257-5v", "257-6v" and "257-7v". Same script and notation.

Interpretation (tentative): leaves from a notated liturgical chant book, cut into strips and pieces and used in a binding. Spellings such as "Evovae" (the vowels of the psalm-tone ending formula, which appears here repeatedly in the text line) and frequent "alleluia" suggest antiphons with psalm-tone cues. That is a genre observation only. I did not try to identify the specific office or feast.

I could not separate lemma from commentary: this is sung text, not glossed text.

======================================================================
FACE C - RECTO PIECES
======================================================================

--- Strip "257-2r" (image-019 overview; read at native resolution in tiles 020, 023, 026, 029, left part) ---
Top edge has a hole and a damaged brown margin. The right edge of the strip is torn, so every line is cut on the right. The left edge appears to be near the column start but also loses letters.

image-020 L1:  n amabilis[...]          ("amabili" clear; final letters at the tear look like "s" or long s)
image-020 L2:  um munc[...]  / "um mu(n)c" - read: "[...]um munc[...]" (could be "mundi"? only "munc" or "mund" visible; uncertain whether the 4th letter is c or d)
image-020 L3:  [...]ua pre[...]
image-023 L1:  [...]sus iohann[...]          (the first letters may be "[...]sus" or "[...]fus"; "iohann" is clear)
image-023 L2:  [...]t alleluia [...]           (one more letter at the right tear, perhaps "E" or "e")
image-023 L3:  P ater [...]                    (large red initial P, two lines high; "ater" in brown with red touch on the a; trace of another letter at the right tear)
image-023 L4 = image-026 L1:  [...]bi nunc [...]   (first visible letters look like "bi" or "hi"; "nunc" clear)
image-026 L2:  [...]ia Evovae [...]          (E of Evovae touched or rubricated in red; end torn)
image-026 L3:  alleluia [red] S?[...]         (a red letter after "alleluia" looks like a long s / S with a red stroke; uncertain)
image-026 L4:  [...]altum all[...]
image-026 L5:  Evovae S[...]                  (large red S begins the next item; the rest is torn)
image-026 L6 = image-029 L1:  [...]e. adorem[...]   (a stop after "e"; "adorem" clear; perhaps "adoremus" but only "adorem" survives)
image-029 L2:  [...]tua sup[...]              (first letter before "ua" may be t or c; "sup" then the tear)
Below this, blank parchment with the pencil shelfmark "Stams, STA, Frg. 257-2r", and the lower end is stained brown.

--- Fragment "257-3r" (top middle in image-019; zoom of tile 021) ---
Heavily damaged by insect holes. Only the top and bottom lines are legible.
image-021 L1:  [...]ren alleluia [...] la Et u[...]    (reading uncertain at the left edge: "[...]rcn" or "[...]ren"; then "alleluia" mostly clear, then a gap, then "[...]la", then E capital touched in red, "Et u[...]")
middle lines:  [illegible] - holes; isolated letters "b", "u" visible
image-021 bottom line (about L4):  [...]sed expectan[...]   ("sed" and "expecta[n]" visible; letters after that are uncertain)

--- Fragment "257-4r" (top right in image-019; tile 022) ---
Two pieces are mounted together, with a small strip sewn or overlapped on the right.
image-022 L1 (left piece):  [...]ust et oc[...]        ("[...]ust" or "[...]ist"; "et oc" clear)
image-022 L1 (right piece): [...]n dn(m)o[...] -> "[...]n d(omi)no" with a macron over the n ("dno" with an abbreviation stroke)
image-022 L2 (left piece):  red rubric "R" with a cross-stroke (the responsory sign Ꝝ / R̷), centre
image-022 L2 (right piece): Evovae
image-022 L3 (left piece):  [...]ita ap[...] / "[...]rita ap[...]" (uncertain; blue-grey staining over the letters)
image-022 L3 (right piece): [...]pa[...]
image-022 L4:  [...]alle   lu[...]   [...]parens[...]    ("alle lu[ia]" split by damage; then "parens" clear, possibly "parent[...]"/"parens e")

--- Fragment "257-5r" (middle left in image-019; tile 024 / zoom of 027) ---
Mostly stained and abraded.
Top lines: [illegible]
image-027 bottom line:  [...]ce eferun[...] / "[...]c[.]eferunt" - I read "[...]ceferun[t?]" but the first letters are uncertain ("ce", "se"?). Below this, a red ruling line.

--- Fragment "257-6r" (middle right in image-019; tile 028) ---
Mostly blank or abraded above. Only the bottom line is legible:
image-028 bottom L1:  [...]a dn(m)s nus? [...]  then red stroke, then "Dominus" with a large red-touched D
   detail: "[...]a dn̄s n̄s" (d n s with abbreviation strokes, i.e. "d(omi)n(u)s n(ost)er"? - expansion uncertain), then a red flourish, then "Dominus" ("D" with a red ascender), with the end of the word partly faded ("Dominu[s]").

--- Fragment "257-7r" (bottom middle in image-019; zoom of tile 027) ---
image-027 L1 (top edge, cut):  [...]ciat[...]   [...]pa[...]   (letter tops only; very uncertain)
rest: stained, with grey adhesive; [illegible]

======================================================================
FACE D - VERSO PIECES
======================================================================

--- Strip "257-2v" (tiles 033, 036, 039, 042, left) ---
Left edge torn. Text is faint and abraded.
image-033 L1:  [...]n [...] f[...]        (isolated letters)
image-033 L2:  [...]c a [red a/rubric] [...]  (a brown "c" or "t" with a red letter "a" touching it; uncertain)
image-033 L3:  [red] P s? [...]           (red initial-like "P", followed by brown "s"; could be a psalm cue "Ps"; uncertain)
image-033 L4 = image-036 L1:  [...]oni[...]a ... / "[...]onn a [...]" (perhaps "[...]onem"; uncertain)
image-036 L2:  [...]is lo[...]
image-036 L3:  [...]dent[...] / "[...]derit[...]"  (uncertain)
image-036 L4:  [...]n abo[...] / "[...]n abe[...]"  (uncertain)
image-036 L5 = image-039 L1:  [...]pre[...] / "[...]pte" or "[...]prie"; "pre" with a following "e"? -> read "[...]pre[.]"
image-039 L2:  [...]ati[...] / "[...]nth[...]"  (uncertain)
image-039 L3:  [...]& le[...]  ("&" or "et" ligature, then "le")
image-039 L4:  [...]t no[...]
image-039 L5:  [...]egre[...] / "[...]agre"  (uncertain)
image-039 L6 = image-042 L1:  red initial, two strokes (looks like "R"/"B" or a red "I" with a bowl) over a black "u" -> [red initial] u[...]
image-042 L2:  [...]du n[...]  ("du" then a gap or stop, then "n")
Below: blank, with the pencil shelfmark "Stams, STA, Frg. 257-2v".

--- Fragment "257-3v" (tiles 033 right and 034 left) ---
